extra.message: User-controlled data from request body or query parameter is deserialized via pickle.loads(). This allows remote code execution via crafted pickle payloads.
User input from request.GET['expr'] is passed directly to eval(). This allows arbitrary Python code execution.

User-controlled template string from request.GET['fragment'] is compiled and rendered via jinja2.Template(). An attacker can craft a template exploiting Jinja2 template injection to read files or achieve RCE via the {{ config }} or {{ config.__class__.__mro__ }} expressions.

User-controlled JSON payload (request.body) is used directly as the MongoDB query filter in find_one(). Without sanitization, an attacker can inject operators like $gt, $ne, or $where for NoSQL injection enabling authentication bypass, data exfiltration, or data manipulation.

User-controlled parameter 'lane' (from request.GET) is passed directly to django.shortcuts.redirect(). An attacker can craft a link like /ops/after/payroll-wayback-card-105/?lane=https://evil.com to perform an open redirect.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: User-supplied 'ref' parameter is used unsanitized in file path BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f'{ref}.json'. An attacker can supply path traversal sequences (e.g., '../../etc/passwd') in 'ref' to write to arbitrary paths on the filesystem.

User-supplied parameter 'name' from request.GET is used without sanitization in the file path BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name. An attacker can inject path traversal sequences (e.g., '../../etc/passwd') to overwrite files on the filesystem when write_bytes() is called on line 180.

The endpoint writes sensitive data including SSN and credit card numbers (with hardcoded defaults: SSN '111-22-3333', card '4111111111111111') into a file based on user input. The file path is derived from user-supplied 'ref' parameter without sanitization, creating a file write that can both traverse directories and store sensitive PII.

Request body (wire_text) and authorization header (request.headers.get('authorization')) are logged via logger.warning(). Sensitive data submitted to this endpoint, including potential authentication credentials, is written to log output in plaintext.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: HTTPS connections to partner.invalid are made with ssl._create_unverified_context() which disables TLS certificate verification, allowing man-in-the-middle attacks.

Value from request.headers.get('origin') (user-controlled) is echoed back into Access-Control-Allow-Origin header. Combined with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: 'true', this allows any origin to make cross-domain authenticated requests.

X-XSS-Protection header is set to '0' and Content-Security-Policy is set to empty string, explicitly disabling browser security features (XSS Auditor and CSP) that would otherwise protect against XSS and click-jacking attacks.

The cookie 'portal_crumb' is set from user input (request.GET['marker']) without any SameSite, Secure, or httponly attributes. This cookie is sent with cross-site requests and contains user-controlled content, enabling XSS-based cookie theft.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in 'Secure' HTTP Cookie Header Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: The endpoint exposes DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE environment variable, BASE_EXPORT_DIR path, and internal trace state to any authenticated user. This leaks internal environment configuration and paths.
Error details including full exception message, traceback info, and BASE_EXPORT_DIR are returned to the client via JsonResponse. Attackers can use these error messages for reconnaissance.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The payroll_mongo_lane_714 endpoint returns repr(doc)[:200] of a MongoDB document query result. Combined with the NoSQL injection vulnerability, an attacker can extract full document contents.

The rendered Jinja template output is returned as text/html without any escaping. Combined with the template injection vulnerability, attacker-controlled content can be reflected in the HTML response as reflected XSS.

Raw API key (raw_key) generated with secrets.token_urlsafe is included in the messages.success() flash message string. If the flash message framework stores messages in database or logs, the raw key would be exposed.

cwe: CWE-359: Exposure of Private Personal Information

extra.message: The api_employees endpoint is decorated with @csrf_exempt, returning employee data (names, emails, departments) for any authenticated user or API key holder. Without CSRF protection, an attacker could forge a request from a victim's browser.
The api_employee_detail endpoint is decorated with @csrf_exempt. An attacker could forge a CSRF request to make a victim read another employee's data through this endpoint.
The api_compensation endpoint is decorated with @csrf_exempt. An attacker could forge a CSRF request to enumerate all compensation records.
The api_documents endpoint is decorated with @csrf_exempt. An attacker could forge a CSRF request to enumerate all document metadata.
DEBUG is set to True by default ('True') when the DEBUG environment variable is not explicitly set. In production, this exposes stack traces, SECRET_KEY, and other debug information to attackers.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Default database password 'hrpayroll123' is hardcoded in settings. If environment variables are not set, this default password will be used, which is easily guessable.

The internal gateway check (_wrk_gate) relies on a single static environment variable comparison (x-internal-token header matching INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN). If the token is leaked or brute-forced, all 19 internal operations become accessible.

The identity verification endpoint returns different error messages ('unknown handle' status 404 vs 'bad verifier' status 403), allowing timing-based or response-code-based enumeration of valid handles and verifiers.
The payroll_bundle_thaw_186 endpoint returns repr(bundle)[:200] of a deserialized object from user-controlled data. This leaks object contents back to the client.

Error details from RuntimeError containing the 'lot_ref' query parameter value are returned to the client in the error response. The BASE_EXPORT_DIR path is also exposed via the error message string in the exception.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
